Marathon Petroleum has fallen 2.6% today, extending a sharp slide over the past week that's left the stock down 8% since November 16th. The decline tracks a broad unwinding of the refinery trade that peaked earlier this year—a CNBC headline explicitly noted today that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding"—suggesting investors are rotating out of energy infrastructure plays after an extended rally. While U.S. oil prices at $89.53 a barrel remain reasonably firm and U.S. refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity, the momentum has shifted away from the sector.

The timing matters: the selloff accelerated just as a U.N. climate summit collapsed without including fossil fuels in its final deal, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, Iranian drone incidents) remain volatile but have not escalated into supply disruptions. The combination of a cooling investment thesis and uncertainty about how long energy strength will persist appears to be driving the outflow.
